chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Abd al-Malik ibn Amr, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Qunut (supplication) before the Ruku' (bowing) or after it. He said, 'No, neither before it nor after it.'
ai.seo_question: When is the Qunut supplication performed in Shia prayer?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific timing of the Qunut supplication by negating its performance before or after the Ruku', thereby establishing its canonical position after rising from Ruku' (Qiyam after Ruku'). This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential preference for the Qunut to be recited in the second Rak'ah during the standing position, distinguishing it from the Sunni practice of reciting it before Ruku' in Witr or after Ruku' in Fajr. The hadith underscores the precision required in the ritual structure of Salah, ensuring that voluntary supplications do not disrupt the established sequence of pillars.
